## Scope, custodian and dictionary

This is a maintained coverage catalogue, not the master document register or an
ISO conformity matrix. Custodian: IMS implementation manager, unassigned. P01–P23
are retained project identities. Their titles identify scope only; descriptions
and starter content below are original drafting. No private source requirements
or methods are exported. The four fundamentals, ten elements, twelve planned
internal standards and four deployment layers are not renumbered or claimed complete.

Fields: process ID = stable existing identity; title = scope label; coverage =
current authoring state; starter = actual supplied file; output = intended evidence;
remaining work = gap, not a waived requirement. A planned entry has no implemented
procedure by implication. Five kits cover parts of four process identities.

## Implementation order and cross-system gaps

First configure P01/P04/P08/P20. Next prioritize the real organization's work and
exposure; do not postpone urgent legal or safety controls until a template exists.
Develop P02/P03/P05/P06/P07 alongside operating processes, then connect P18/P19/P21/P22
to evidence and improvement. Customer/provider and controlled-operation cases are
the next public authoring tranche, followed by environmental/OH&S and continuity cases.

| Adoption area | Starting dependencies | Still needed before a completeness claim |
|---|---|---|
| Quality | P09–P13, P17–P19, P21 | Customer change, design applicability, provider/production/release criteria, measurement and real results |
| Environment | P01, P11–P12, P14, P16, P18, P21–P22 | Site-specific aspects, obligations, lifecycle influence, operating/emergency controls and evaluations |
| Occupational health and safety | P03, P06, P11–P12, P15–P16, P18, P21–P22 | Worker participation, hazards, hierarchy decisions, competent work/contractor controls and effectiveness |
| Continuity | P01, P04–P07, P11–P12, P16, P18–P23 | Business impact analysis, critical dependencies, recovery objectives, strategies, plans, exercises and evaluation |

Maintenance is a cross-process capability, especially P05/P11/P12/P15/P22/P23,
not a silently added P24. A leaking-valve story needs notification/triage, competent
assessment, work authorization, planning, technical isolation/repair criteria,
verification, handback and learning; those technical templates are **not supplied**
by the five administrative kits. A CMMS can hold linked evidence, but is not required
to use this document library and is not implemented here.

## Entry, update, access and retention rules

Use each P identity once; do not renumber to match clauses or create a new process
merely for a new form. Add actual document links only after authoring/registering
them. On a changed coverage claim, preserve the assessed prior catalogue, increment
revision, record the source/destination and check links and receiving owners.
Duplicate IDs, broken links and “complete” without scoped evidence are invalid.
Adopters add their applicability reason, owner, gap/action ID and evidence in a
private implementation view; it does not overwrite this published learning catalogue.
Preserve history and access controls under the document-control procedure; no
automatic disposal. Review on new kits, scope changes and user findings.

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.

r01 — 2026-11-01: initial original beginner-kit draft. Actual appointments,
competent review, representative user trial, approval and effectiveness pending.
Fictional decisions never authorize real work. Editable renditions, where supplied,
share this identity/revision; this Markdown is the master. Record a new derivative
identity/configuration when adapting, and reconcile changes before release.
